findings.description: Transfer does not rollback account balances if ledger.record raises ValueError, violating the specification that requires both accounts and the ledger to remain unchanged when the ledger rejects the entry.
findings.evidence: Example: accounts={"a":10,"b":0}, memo="x"*41 (41 chars). Calling transfer(accounts, ledger, "a", "b", 5, memo) will cause ledger.record to raise ValueError, but accounts become {"a":5,"b":5} and ledger.entries stays []. This violates the required atomicity and leaves state inconsistent.

review.summary: Candidate implementation fails to maintain atomicity when ledger rejects the entry; account balances are modified before ledger.record and are not rolled back, violating the contract that requires the ledger and accounts to remain unchanged if ledger.record raises ValueError.
